blocks.prompt: 9 The members of a club are 10 boys and 8 girls. In how many ways can a committee of 6 boys and 3 girls be formed?
blocks.explanation:
A committee is a selection, so order does not matter.
We must choose 6 of the 10 boys and 3 of the 8 girls together.
Plan: \({}^{10}C_{6} \times {}^{8}C_{3}\).
steps:
Given: 10 boys, 8 girls; committee of 6 boys and 3 girls.
To find: the number of committees.
Method: Boys and girls are chosen separately (combinations), then multiplied because both choices are made together.

Choose the boys
\[{}^{10}C_{6} = {}^{10}C_{4}\]
\[= \dfrac{10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 \cdot 7}{4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{5040}{24} = 210\]
Why: Choosing 6 boys to take is the same as choosing 4 to leave out, and 4 factors are quicker than 6.

Choose the girls
\[{}^{8}C_{3} = \dfrac{8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6}{3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1} = 56\]
Why: 3 girls out of 8.

Multiply
\[210 \times 56 = 200 \times 56 + 10 \times 56\]
\[= 11200 + 560 = 11760\]
Why: Every choice of boys can go with every choice of girls.

Check
\[11760 \div 56 = 210 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Dividing back gives the boys' count.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints 1176. This is a misprint (a zero is missing): \({}^{10}C_{6} \times {}^{8}C_{3} = 210 \times 56 = 11760\). The correct answer is 11,760.
